subject: ZephyrGrid late-stage capacity readiness & fleet gating
messages:
From: Zoe Kim <zoe.kim@zephyrgrid.io>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Torres <alex@zephyrgrid.io>, procurement@zephyrgrid.io
Date: 2028-09-07T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps for ZephyrGrid procurement

Monica —

Thanks for the walkthrough today. We're targeting an enterprise launch in mid-November and need a firm plan for dedicated capacity. Our architects estimate a baseline of 48 A100-equivalent GPUs with burst capacity to 72 for peak onboarding. Before we escalate to procurement, can Redwood confirm you can gate that capacity in the us-west region and list fallback options if a partial pool is delayed?

Also attaching our internal traffic ramp and a sample contract. We prefer a single vendor contract but need explicit SLAs around preemption, regional availability, and data residency.

Best,
Zoe Kim
CTO, ZephyrGrid Inc.
[attachment: zg_q4_capacity_matrix.csv]

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Zoe Kim <zoe.kim@zephyrgrid.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-09-07T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps for ZephyrGrid procurement

Zoe —

Appreciate the details and the matrix. Short answer: we can provision a committed pool sized to 48 GPUs in us-west as a Dedicated reservation and provide burst headroom to 72 across our dedicated+hosted hybrid routing policy, with explicit fallbacks to us-east and our dedicated overflow cluster (quantum-pool).

Next steps I propose:
- Ben/infra to run a live availability sweep for the target November window and mark a soft hold on 48 GPUs in us-west for two weeks while legal finalizes SOWs.
- Karthik to map latency/cost tradeoffs for fallback routing (us-east vs quantum-pool) and confirm SLA delta for burst.
- I'll coordinate with procurement to align DocuSign flow.

I'll loop in Grace for the runbook and Sean for escalation points. If any of you need different owners for those tasks, flag here.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
[attachment: Zephyr_Contract_Draft_v3.pdf]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-09-08T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps for ZephyrGrid procurement

Team —

I ran the inventory sweep across us-west for the Nov 10 - Nov 30 onboarding window. Quick summary:
- 48 A100-equivalent GPUs: available as dedicated reservation in us-west-2, but two nodes overlap with scheduled maintenance on Nov 18-19 
- Additional 24 GPUs (to reach 72 burst): available via dedicated overflow in our quantum-pool (cross-region) with an expected latency penalty of ~12-18ms P95 compared to pure us-west routing
- No competing soft-holds in the same window currently — recommended: place a soft hold on 48 units and a conditional hold on the extra 24 until contract signature.

Action items I already started:
1) Opened ticket INF-2028-379 for the maintenance conflict to request slight reschedule or migration to spare nodes.
2) Created temporary resource hold ticket HOLD-2028-912 (48 GPUs, us-west-2, 14 days) — requires manager approval to convert to committed reservation.

I'll attach the raw inventory CSV to the ticket. Ping me if you want me to escalate maintenance now rather than wait for legal.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Capacity Operations, Redwood Inference
[attachment: inventory_snapshot_us-west-20280908.csv]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-09-08T14:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps for ZephyrGrid procurement

Folks —

I ran a quick latency/cost delta analysis for the fallback options. Highlights:
- us-east fallback: additional ~7ms P95, cost +8% on token compute due to cross-region egress and syncing KV caches.
- quantum-pool (overflow): additional ~15ms P95, cost +5% compute but with potential higher operational variance during peak due to shared tenancy.

Recommendation: confirm the 48 GPU hold in us-west and accept conditional overflow for the 24 burst. Add a clause in the SOW that requires Redwood to notify ZephyrGrid 72 hours before activating cross-region overflow for sustained >75% utilization for longer than 6 hours. That gives ZephyrGrid time to postpone heavy onboarding tasks or provision alternative fallbacks.

I'll populate the clause text for legal to attach to the SOW. Also flagging that if maintenance INF-2028-379 cannot be rescheduled, we should mark two spare nodes in us-west as warm standby to avoid churn.

-Karthik
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Zoe Kim <zoe.kim@zephyrgrid.io>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-09-09T16:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps for ZephyrGrid procurement

Hi Zoe —

Thanks for the detailed ask and the patience. We placed HOLD-2028-912 as a two-week soft hold for 48 GPUs in us-west-2 today and opened INF-2028-379 for maintenance mitigation. Attached is a brief runbook excerpt showing notification cadence and escalation contacts if overflow is triggered.

A couple of notes for contract language and SLAs:
- We can guarantee the 48-unit reserved pool with our standard Dedicated SLA. Any activation of overflow (quantum-pool/us-east) will follow the 72-hour notification policy Karthik proposed.
- If ZephyrGrid needs absolute single-region exclusivity, we can offer a regional exclusivity addendum but it requires a 6–8 week lead time for capacity earmarking and a minimum commitment term.

Next steps for ZephyrGrid:
1) Sign the SOW/DocuSign so we can convert HOLD-2028-912 to a committed reservation.
2) Decide whether to accept conditional overflow for burst or request the exclusivity addendum (we can provide pricing for both).
3) If you want us to contest INF-2028-379 maintenance now, say the word and we'll put operations on expedited schedule.

Zoe — happy to hop on a 20-minute call if you'd like to walk the runbook.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Ops Lead, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
